## Client Config
This is the ONLY file you should need to edit per client.

Duplicate this whole template folder per client, then edit the values below (and swap credentials in each workflow's nodes to that client's Twilio / Vapi / Google / SMTP accounts).

Every other workflow calls this one via "Execute Sub-Workflow" to pull these values - never hardcode client details anywhere else.

managerPhoneNumber (uncertainty transfer): the live number the Vapi assistant transfers a call to mid-conversation when the caller's request doesn't match any known job type/pricing/booking scenario - separate from receptionForwardNumber's existing SIP-failure fallback (technical breakdown, not confusion). This value is NOT read dynamically by Vapi at call time (the assistant's tools are static, configured once in the Vapi dashboard/API, not fetched from n8n per call) - it's the canonical source you copy into the assistant's transfer_to_manager tool destination when creating/updating the assistant, same manual-sync pattern already used for vapiSipCredentialId. Leave blank to fall back to receptionForwardNumber as that same tool's destination (see vapi-assistant-config.json and the README for why).

reportingSheetId/callLogTabName (Monthly Reporting): this client's own Google Sheet where every call's outcome gets logged (03-post-call-actions writes one row per call, regardless of outcome) - this is the only historical record of call volume/bookings in the whole system, read later by workflows/monthly-reporting. Also copy this same sheet ID (plus this client's jobsSheetId from the Invoice Automation Client Config) into the shared Clients Registry sheet's row for this client - see workflows/monthly-reporting/README.md for why that's a separate, synced copy rather than a live lookup.

quoteConfig/quoteLogTabName (Quoting Engine): quoteConfig is this client's structured job-type/pricing rulebook, looked up by the new get_quote tool in 02-vapi-tools (see that file's sticky note) so quotes come from real config data, never an AI-invented number. The example below is realistic mock pricing for a fictional UK plumbing/heating business - replace jobTypes, calloutFee, hourlyRateOutsideStandardJobs, emergencyMultiplier and emergencyHours with the real client's actual rules; the matching/pricing/logging logic itself does not change. hourlyRateOutsideStandardJobs is stored for the business's own reference only - the current fallback logic deliberately never uses it to invent a price for an unmatched job (see requirement 4 in the task, and the README). quoteLogTabName is the tab in this client's reportingSheetId where every quote given gets logged (matched or fallback) - same sheet as callLogTabName, different tab, so both logs live in one place per client.
